messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Your list is mostly right. I haven’t agreed to A’s discounted purchase, and I won’t subsidize it; I want a fair financial share. I don’t know whether B needs money. I’d consider a purchase on fair, clearly established terms, with all three of us heard and no pressure to sign. I don’t know what the will says, who is handling the estate, or whether there’s a valuation or deadline. I’m not in a hurry.

Thanks. The list is broadly right. I want a financially workable path toward independence, and hope to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I can’t say what price is fair until there’s a valuation and clear terms; I don’t want C to subsidize the purchase, and I need her agreement to proceed. I don’t know what the will says, who is handling the estate, or whether there’s a deadline or valuation. I know B wants money, but not why.

Thank you for asking. I do need money to start a dance studio, though I don’t yet know what amount or arrangement would be possible. I don’t know the will terms, who’s handling the estate, any deadline, or whether the house has been valued. I’d appreciate being included in a fair, pressure-free process.

I don’t object to your NCEs or the process draft. By financially workable, I mean being able to buy without taking on more than we can afford. I still hope for a discount, but I can’t say how that avoids reducing C’s share until we know the valuation and how everyone’s shares are treated. Clear terms would include the price, each sister’s share, and the timing. I don’t know who has the will or is handling the estate; I can ask the family. Knowing B wants a dance studio doesn’t change my view that she should be heard in a fair process.

Your NCEs seem reasonable to me. Being included would mean hearing the same information and having my studio need considered before anything is decided. I’d want the will, estate handler and valuation checked, with no pressure to sign. I don’t know what money arrangement would work yet, but I can accept a slower decision while the facts are checked.

I agree with the weighing and process. Fair terms need an independent valuation agreed by all three, a clear price and timing, and an explicit account of who gives up any value; I won’t subsidize A’s purchase. A fair share means I receive my proper financial share, though I can’t define the legal amount yet. I’m fine with A asking about the will and estate handler. Share the valuation and proposed terms with all three before anyone decides.

That NCE is right. I’ll ask the family now who has the will and is handling the estate. We could agree together on an independent valuer, so none of us chooses them alone. I don’t disagree with the process draft.

I agree that affordability should be addressed without reducing any sister’s share. Please include that my studio need should be considered once the facts are known, though I don’t yet know the amount I’d need. I’m not sure who could provide a valuation; perhaps all three of us could agree on an independent valuer.
